newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair attacks Major over Europe.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair attacks Major over Europe.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair, opinion poll favourite to win Thursday's general election, accused Prime Minister John Major of a "pitiful" performance in Europe.
Blair said his party would stand up for British interests and it was "nonsense" for Major to claim that he alone could negotiate successfully for Britain in Europe.
"Judge him on his track record," Blair wrote in an article appearing in Thursday's edition of The European newspaper.
"The story of the ban on British beef is one of incompetence, hollow aggression and unending failure."
The Labour leader said: "Our position on Europe is not seriously challenged from any quarter of the party, whereas John Major has led his party pitifully."
Blair said there were three choices open to Britain -- leaving the European Union, staying in but impotent, or staying in and leading.
Blair said he rejected the first choice and said the second was where Britain was now under the Conservatives: "powerless and committed to following the decisions of others".
"I would not be willing to sacrifice Britain's economic future and status in the world by leaving the EU and opting for permanent isolationism."
He added: "We must stand up for Britain's interests and be prepared to stand alone in support of these interests if necessary. But we achieve nothing from perpetual isolation.
"In and leading is where we want to be and then we can have a real say in where Europe is going."
Blair said he wanted a Europe where national identities are not submerged and where countries cooperage, "not a giant unmanageable super-state, run from the centre".
